messages.subject: Re: Types of sums of Squares...
messages.body_plain:
I don't like type I ssq at all, but you should be able to use them if
you wish. I will implement this next time I alter the modeling dialogs
(which may be some time from now). As a general design principle I'd
like to stay away from preferences that change the default types of
analysis because then users can perform the same actions and get
different results.

ian

>
> Deducer is a great GUI, and I love the new ggplot2 GUI!  Superb work.
>
> I hate to bring up such a controversial old chestnut, but would it be
> possible to include Type I sums of squares as an option in Deducer's
> modelling facilities?  And, if not already available in Deducer, the
> ability to set a particular type as a default option for all relevant
> analyses?
>
> There is a sizeable community of statisticians who strongly prefer the
> logic of the Type I sum of squares - I would like to present Deducer
> as a useful R GUI to others within my organisation, but the lack of

> I can appreciate the conservative nature of the Type II SS in the
> context of ANOVA (I.e., analysis of designed experiments with

>
> Cheers,

> Alec Zwart

messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 gui / plotbuilder feedback
messages.body_plain:
Hi Matt,

While very prevalent in the psychometric world, it may not be of
universal interest. I will include a dialog in the DeducerExtras
package in the next version. Below is the implementation using a new,
second, as of yet undocumented, plug-in interface.

Cheers,
Ian

########################################################################
#
#				Intraclass correlation coefficient
#
########################################################################
.makeICCDialog <- function(){
	require(irr)
	iccFunc <- new(RFunction,"icc")

	ratingsParam <- new(ParamMultipleVariables,"ratings")
	iccFunc$add(ratingsParam)

	modelParam <- new(ParamCharacter,"model","oneway")
	modelParam$setOptions(c("oneway", "twoway"))
	modelParam$setViewType(modelParam$VIEW_COMBO)
	iccFunc$add(modelParam)

	typeParam <- new(ParamCharacter,"type","consistency")
	typeParam$setOptions(c("consistency", "agreement"))
	typeParam$setViewType(typeParam$VIEW_COMBO)
	iccFunc$add(typeParam)

	unitParam <- new(ParamCharacter,"unit","single")
	unitParam$setOptions(c("single", "average"))
	unitParam$setViewType(unitParam$VIEW_COMBO)
	iccFunc$add(unitParam)

	nullParam <- new(ParamNumeric,"r0")
	nullParam$setTitle("H0")
	nullParam$setValue(0)
	nullParam$setLowerBound(0)
	iccFunc$add(nullParam)

	conf <- new(ParamNumeric,"conf.level",.95)
	conf$setLowerBound(0)
	conf$setUpperBound(1)
	iccFunc$add(conf)

	rfd <- new(RFunctionDialog, iccFunc)
	rfd$setSize(425L,500L)
	rfd$setLocationRelativeTo(.jnull())
	rfd
}

require(DeducerExtras)
.makeICCDialog()$run()

messages.subject: Added Functionality to Deducer's Plotting GUI
messages.subject_clean: Added Functionality to Deducer's Plotting GUI
messages.body_plain:
Hello Ian,

First of all, I want to congratulate you on your GUI implementation of
the ggplot2 graphing package. I think your choice of the ggplot system
will make Deducer a successful GUI to the R program.

I am in the middle of writing a continuing professional development
course in exploratory data analysis that will be offered primarily to
property appraisers. The software we chose for the course will be a
combination of Excel and R. We intend to use RExcel to allow
spreadsheet data to be passed to R where students will primarily use
the plotting function. At this time, it is my thought to use Deducer
as a GUI to R.

In experimenting with Deducer, there is some functionality available
in R Commander that I could not find in Deducer at this time. Could
you please tell me if the following is on your list to add to Deducer:

a) The ability to save plots in various image file forms such as JPEG,
PNG, PDF, etc.

b) the ability to copy the script used to generate a plot so that it
can be pasted in a Word document.

Thank you again for your wonderful contribution to the R system.

Charles Abromaitis

messages.subject: Re: New Deducer Plugin
messages.body_plain:
I think it would be a good idea to do that as the number of Plug-ins
gets larger. The R/JGR/Deducer plug-in will install all plug-ins by
default.

As far as naming schemes go. My preference is to camel cased names
starting with Deducer. There is the Extras package, which is named
DeducerExtras, and the Plug-in Example package is
DeducerPlugInExample. There is no need to insert 'Plugin' into the
name, as it is obvious that anything starting with 'Deducer' is an
add-on. The . separator that Rcmdr uses just doesn't speak to me.

Also, think about using full words for your plug-in's name rather than acronyms.

I'm not going to enforce any naming conventions for plug-in packages,
but I would highly recommend that the name starts with Deducer. This
is so that the package is listed next to all of the other plug-ins in
the installer dialog.

I will enforce Plug-in inter-compatability. All plug-ins should work
with one another. If your plug-in breaks another plug-in, it will not
be included in the standard install (not really a big deal though).

That's my two cents on the topic.

Ian

messages.subject: Deducer 0.4-1 and JGR 1.7-2 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I would like to announce the release of Deducer 0.4-1 and JGR 1.7-2 to
CRAN. The updates should be propagating through the mirrors over the
next few days. On the Deducer side we have a number of nice
improvements:

1. A new Text Field Widget for plug-ins is included, which is better
suited for entering/displaying numeric and short string fields than
TextAreaWidget.
2. A new Object Chooser Widget is included, which allows the user to
select an object from their workspace, possibly of a specific class.
3. Fixed combobox bug on Mac OS 64-bit.
4. Factor editor and Recode dialog handle empty strings.
5. Created menu items for common templates.

The new JGR includes stability fixes along with a few new features.

Bug fixes:
1. Fixed MacOS JavaGD resize deadlock bug
2. Fixed 100% CPU on start-up bug reported on some UNIX systems.
3. Interrupt R button fixed on unix systems

New Features:
1. Graphics device save support for png, jpeg, bmp, and tiff
2. User control over the menu system has been improved. Added ability
to insert new menus, menu items, separators, and sub-menus. Menus and
menu items can also be removed.

Ian Fellows

On 25 Set, 18:56, Ian Fellows <ifell...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi All,
>
> I would like to announce the release of Deducer 0.4-1 and JGR 1.7-2 to
> CRAN. The updates should be propagating through the mirrors over the
> next few days. On the Deducer side we have a number of nice
> improvements:
>
> 1. A new Text Field Widget for plug-ins is included, which is better
> suited for entering/displaying numeric and short string fields than
> TextAreaWidget.
> 2. A new Object Chooser Widget is included, which allows the user to
> select an object from their workspace, possibly of a specific class.
> 3. Fixed combobox bug on Mac OS 64-bit.
> 4. Factor editor and Recode dialog handle empty strings.
> 5. Created menu items for common templates.
>
> The new JGR includes stability fixes along with a few new features.
>
> Bug fixes:
> 1. Fixed MacOS JavaGD resize deadlock bug
> 2. Fixed 100% CPU on start-up bug reported on some UNIX systems.
> 3. Interrupt R button fixed on unix systems
>
> New Features:
> 1. Graphics device save support for png, jpeg, bmp, and tiff
> 2. User control over the menu system has been improved. Added ability
> to insert new menus, menu items, separators, and sub-menus. Menus and
> menu items can also be removed.
>
> Ian Fellows

messages.subject: Re: feature request, subset in plot builder
messages.subject_clean: feature request, subset in plot builder
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Ian,

Thanks for you quick fix on the empty strings, it works well now.

For the subset in plot though, I'd hesitate to create multiple
data.frames just for plotting purpose. For many (all?) "Genometric
Elements", you have an "Options" panel, which seems to have a lot of
space to put more stuff in?? (a text box will be suffice to me
compared with a full blown subset builder...)

Thanks again.

Wenjian

On Sep 23, 4:41 pm, Ian Fellows <ifell...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Wenjian,
>
> > 1) it is helpful for me to be able to have a subset textbox in the
> > plot builder, similar to the "subset" in analysis dialogs already.
>
> To subset your plots you have two options. first, you can do the
> subset first by using the subset dialog. Secondly, you can specify the
> data range in the scale_* for any aesthetic. Since each layer can have
> its own dataset, adding a subset chooser in each layer would add
> additional complexity to an already busy window.
>
>
>
> > 2a) The "Factor Editor" is not listing empty strings if it's one of
> > the levels. For example, if I have a variable with factor levels ("",
> > "A", "B", "C"), it seems to the "Factor Editor" can only remove "A",
> > "B", "C", but not "", since "" doesn't show up.
>
> Thank you. Fixed in development.
>
>
>
> > 2b) Similarly if it can be easier to recode "" (or others) into NA in
> > the "Recode Variable" dialogs.
>
> Fixed in development.
>
>
>
> > 2c) An "as.is <http://as.is>" option and "na.string" choices in the "Read File"
> > dialog?
>
> Good idea. I've put this on a new feature request page. (http://www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.FeatureRequests)
>
>
>
> > 3) I think it's mentioned before in the discussion about survival
> > analysis and KM plots. Not sure if it's already available, but I could
> > try to create the plugin if not.
>
> That would be great. I would be more than happy to support your effort.
>
>
>
> > Some more functions in the Data Viewer, e.g. sorting and filtering,
> > would be helpful too, but I'm sure they will be there in future
> > versions.
>
> agreed. Now on the feature request page.
>
> Cheers,
> Ian
